correctness.rationale: For j<p, either the maximizing mean at j is at most f(j+1), or it uses r≥1. The ball at j+1 of radius r−1 has the same clipped right endpoint; the only removed sites lie at or to the left of j and have values below the old mean. Hence Mf cannot decrease before p; reflection gives the other branch. Singleton values and the global maximum give Mf(p)=f(p), including every permissible p on a plateau. Both variations then telescope. The prefix and suffix through p lift the endpoint values by at least A/(p+1) and B/(n−p). Subtracting (A+B)/n gives the exact claimed lower bound on the deficit. For nonconstant data an interior p makes that lower bound strictly positive. If the peak is the first endpoint, equality forces the global mean at the opposite endpoint to attain its baseline-plus-one-spike lower bound, which forces every nonpeak value to be the baseline; reflection handles the last endpoint. A spike realizes equality. A decrease followed by an increase prevents unimodality and yields separated boundary or interior peaks (allowing plateaux). For signed inputs apply the inequality to the modulus and use the reverse triangle inequality, without extending the equality classification. The exact finite checker was inspected, not executed; it selects the first maximum, so the all-permissible-index assertion rests on the proof.
residual_risks: The argument is confined to counting-measure paths, centered graph balls and edge 1-variation; it does not prove the unrestricted conjecture.
